input.command:
cat > diagnosis.json <<'EOF'
{"spec_element": "invariant",
 "proof_obligation": "bridge",
 "diagnosis": "The loop invariant in FindZero was weakened to `forall k :: 0 <= k < index && k < a.Length - 1 ==> a[k] != 0`, which says nothing about the last element a[a.Length-1]. On exit (index >= a.Length) the invariant therefore does not imply the postcondition `index < 0 ==> forall i :: 0 <= i < a.Length ==> a[i] != 0` (counterexample: a[a.Length-1] == 0). The bound should be `k < a.Length`, which SkippingLemma's postcondition maintains."}
EOF
sed -i '118s/k < (a.Length) - 1/k < a.Length/' program.dfy && sed -n 118p program.dfy && dafny verify program.dfy

content.text:
`program.dfy` now verifies: Dafny reports 21 verified, 0 errors.

**What was wrong:** the loop invariant in `FindZero` (line 118) was too weak. It read:

```dafny
invariant forall k :: 0 <= k < index && k < (a.Length) - 1 ==> a[k] != 0
```

Because of the `- 1`, it said nothing about the last element, `a[a.Length-1]`. When the loop ends with `index >= a.Length`, that invariant can't prove the postcondition that no element is zero when `index < 0`. This matches the counterexample, where `a[7719] = 0` is the last element. So this is an invariant failing at the **bridge** step (invariant plus exit condition don't give the postcondition). I recorded that in `diagnosis.json`.

**The fix:** I changed the bound to `k < a.Length`:

```dafny
invariant forall k :: 0 <= k < index && k < a.Length ==> a[k] != 0
```

The loop still keeps this stronger invariant true, because `SkippingLemma` proves that every element between `index` and the next `index` is non-zero.

**Exit code:** `dafny verify` still exits with code 2. That comes from a warning about unusual indentation at line 160, in code unrelated to this fix. Warnings are treated as errors by default (`--allow-warnings` is false), so the exit code is non-zero even though verification passed. I didn't change that code. Adding parentheses at line 160 would clear the warning, or you can run with `--allow-warnings`.
